notes.title: Patch Notes Ver. 0.4.5
notes.notes:
🔧 Bug Fixes

Fixed an issue where the music would behave erratically when entering the Stage 3 Boss fight.

⚙️ Combat & Balance Adjustments

Increased the chance for “Zero Energy” skills to trigger a 100% cost reduction effect for 3 seconds.

Increased laser damage for the Stage 2 Boss.

All boss damage has been globally increased.

Adjusted bullet patterns for certain enemy types.

🎨 UI Improvements

Door interaction UI is now displayed horizontally instead of vertically for better clarity.

🆕 New Skills (2)

Bouncing Energy Orb: Fires an energy orb in the aimed direction. It bounces upon contact with surfaces, increasing both its speed and damage with each bounce. Lasts up to 3 seconds.

Starburst Impact: Unleashes a powerful explosive blast in a 30-pixel cone in front of you. High burst damage with strong recoil — ideal for close-range combat.

notes.title: Anchors Away: Updates, Changes, and the Next Step for the Submarine
notes.notes:
Ahoy, Divers!

Long time no see! It's been four months in the blink of an eye. For a while, our submarine project was put on hold. Over the past few months, we've run into quite a few challenges—especially personal ones on my end. As a result, we had to find work to stabilize things. But now that life has settled down, development will continue! That said, it'll be at a slower, steady pace as we work on it in our free time.

During this break, I've been reflecting a lot on the game’s overall design. After watching several streamers play, I’ve realized that the game's rules might be a bit too complex—weapon attributes, limited equipment slots, strange skill behaviors, room rewards… all of it together creates a high learning curve. The data also shows that around half of the players leave after about 10 minutes—right around two deaths. That means the game currently lacks a strong enough hook to keep players engaged beyond that point.

I feel like the mechanics are numerous and varied but not well-integrated. So, going forward, I’ll be focusing on refining and simplifying the core design. Here are my three major areas of improvement:

1️⃣ Room Rewards Standardization – Room rewards will become more predictable while still maintaining trade-off mechanics. For example, weapon damage and skill damage will remain in conflict, but they will always appear in the same reward rooms, and room numbers will be fixed.

2️⃣ Unified Item Effects – All item attributes will affect both weapons and skills. However, to balance this, skills will receive additional stat nerfs.

3️⃣ Skill Progression Overhaul – Weapon and skill-related items will be merged into a single "Item" category. Skills will no longer be influenced by items but will instead evolve through level-ups. Each skill can be upgraded only three times, with branching choices. For instance, when upgrading a shield skill, you might have to choose between "Reflective Shield" or "Absorption Shield."

The first change is already in progress, and we're also working on the third stage! I'd love to hear your thoughts—let’s discuss and shape the future of the game together! 🚀

notes.title: 0.3.1 Major Update
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, submarines:

Version 0.3 has finally been updated. This version adds a lot of props, weapons, second levels and bosses, etc.

Major changes:

Each floor's reward room has added a mutual exclusion system. When choosing a different room, the other connected room will be consumed (skills and weapons are mutually exclusive, upgrades and stores are mutually exclusive)

Rooms 1-13 no longer force the multiple growth of the gold room to be interrupted, and the store will be forced to refresh in room 14. (So if you want to choose to upgrade, you need to choose before the 14th)

The core room can always match three skill core props according to the equipped skills. Choose one.

The weapon component changes from a random prop to three choices, and matches according to the growth of the secondary attribute selected by the player.

Now you can choose to buy weapons, skills, skill cores, and weapon core props in the store room.

The effect of re-roll on the prop price is cancelled

Added 2 new skills, Lightning Ball, Hydraulic Blast.

Weapon component modules increased to 40

Modified the first-stage Boss Lunena

notes.title: Demo Version Breakdown
notes.notes:
Hello fellow subs:
I am very happy to discuss the Demo version of SQD. Original plan
It is composed of 4 floors, and only the 1st and 3rd floors have fixed upgrade systems. 
All weapon upgrades and skill upgrades also have components to achieve the same effect, but they require additional equipment slots. 
Therefore, more floors are required to complete. However, the content of the Demo version is not enough to support the monsters and content volume of 4 floors.
In this regard, we have made special prop refresh adjustments for the Demo version. This adjustment will break the strategic nature of the original design.
It's more about luck. In the current Demo version, we have arranged 3 skills, and 20 components and skill cores.
The version is already undergoing technical testing, and the Demo version is expected to be released next week. I hope everyone can have fun playing it.
